questions.prompt: When was the last time you received a gift?
questions.sampleA1:
Gift? Ah... yesterday. My birthday.

My mother give me cake.

I like cake.
questions.sampleA2:
I think last gift... maybe last month?

It was my birthday, and my grandma gave me a sweater.

It was blue and very warm, but I don't like the color very much.

But I said thank you.
questions.sampleB1:
The last time I got a gift was actually a few weeks ago.

It was from my colleague at work.

He was leaving the company, and he gave me a small plant as a goodbye present.

I think it was a nice gesture, and it was unexpected, so it was a good surprise.

I hope I can keep the plant alive!
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, the last gift I got was only a couple of weeks ago, for my birthday. A close friend turned up with a pair of concert tickets, which honestly caught me off guard. I'd been meaning to see that band for ages, so it really made my day. It was such a thoughtful gesture.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Sovg'a? Aha... kecha. Mening tug'ilgan kunim.

Onam menga tort berdi.

Menga tort yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
O'ylashimcha, oxirgi sovg'a... balki o'tgan oy?

Bu mening tug'ilgan kunim edi va buvim menga sviter sovg'a qildi.

U ko'k va juda issiq edi, lekin menga rangi unchalik yoqmadi.

Lekin men rahmat aytdim.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Oxirgi marta sovg‘a olganim bundan bir necha hafta oldin edi.

Bu ishxonadagi hamkasbimdan edi.

U kompaniyadan ketayotgan edi va menga xayrlashuv sovg‘asi sifatida kichik bir gul berdi.

Menimcha, bu yaxshi imo-ishora edi va u kutilmagan edi, shuning uchun bu yaxshi syurpriz bo'ldi.

Umid qilamanki, gulni tirik saqlay olaman!
questions.uzSampleB2:
O'ylab ko'ray... oxirgi marta sovg'a olganim Rojdestvo atrofida bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak.

Singlim menga striming xizmatiga obuna sovg'a qildi, bu men hujjatli filmlarni qanchalik yoqtirishimni hisobga olsak, juda o'rinli edi.

Dastlab, biroz ikkilandim, chunki menda allaqachon bir nechta obunalar bor edi, lekin aslida bu juda foydali ekanligini aniqladim.

Bu menga kengroq kontentga kirish imkonini berdi va u sovg'ani tanlashda mening qiziqishlarimni eslaganidan minnatdorman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - When was the last time you received a gift?...
idioms: bookworm - "kitobxon"
"A room without books is like a body without a soul" - "Kitobsiz xona jonsiz tanaga o'xshaydi"
page-turner - "qiziqarli kitob"
sentenceStarters: "Honestly speaking, I recently received a delightful surprise gift from a dear friend that truly warmed my heart." - "Rostini aytsam, yaqinda yaqin do'stimdan ajoyib kutilmagan sovg'a oldim, bu mening yuragimni chin dildan quvontirdi."

"From my perspective, the last gift I received was a testament to the thoughtfulness and generosity of my family." - "Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, oxirgi marta olgan sovg'am oilamning mulohazakorligi va saxiyligining isboti edi."

"I'd have to say that the most recent gift I received was not only unexpected but also immensely appreciated." - "Shuni aytishim kerakki, yaqinda olgan sovg'am nafaqat kutilmagan, balki juda qadrlanadigan edi."

questions.sampleAnswer: Honestly, the last time I received a gift was just a couple of weeks ago. It was a particularly special occasion as it was my birthday, and one of my closest friends dropped by unexpectedly. She handed me a beautifully wrapped package that caught me off guard and filled me with curiosity. Upon opening it, I discovered a handcrafted journal. Now, this wasn't just any journal; it was incredibly personalized, with my initials embossed on the cover and a collection of our shared memories inside. This gift was truly thoughtful, as it not only catered to my passion for writing but also encapsulated the essence of our long-standing friendship. I must say, receiving such a gift warmed the cockles of my heart. It made me realize how much effort and love she had invested in creating something so meaningful. In today's fast-paced world, where we often rush through our lives, such gestures serve as a gentle reminder to cherish the relationships we hold dear. As the saying goes, "It's the thought that counts," and this experience was a testament to that.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, so'nggi marta sovg'a olganimga atigi ikki hafta bo'ldi. Bu ayniqsa muhim voqea edi, chunki bu mening tug'ilgan kunim edi va eng yaqin do'stlarimdan biri kutilmaganda tashrif buyurdi. U menga chiroyli o'ralgan paketni uzatdi, bu meni hayratga soldi va qiziquvchanlik bilan to'ldirdi.

Uni ochganimdan so'ng, qo'lda yasalgan jurnalni topdim. Bu shunchaki oddiy jurnal emas edi; u juda shaxsiy edi, muqovasida mening ism-sharifimning bosh harflari bosilgan va ichida bizning umumiy xotiralarimiz to'plami bor edi. Bu sovg'a haqiqatan ham o'ylab topilgan edi, chunki u nafaqat yozishga bo'lgan ishtiyoqimga mos keldi, balki uzoq yillik do'stligimiz mohiyatini ham o'zida mujassam etgan edi.

Aytishim kerakki, bunday sovg'ani olish yuragimni iliqlashtirdi. Bu menga uning shunchalik mazmunli narsani yaratishga qancha mehnat va muhabbat sarflaganini anglatdi. Bugungi tez sur'atlar bilan rivojlanayotgan dunyoda, biz ko'pincha hayotimizda shoshilib o'tib ketamiz, bunday imo-ishoralar biz qadrlaydigan munosabatlarni qadrlashga muloyim eslatma bo'lib xizmat qiladi. Aytganlaridek, "Muhimi - niyat", va bu tajriba bunga dalil edi.

questions.prompt: Who was your favourite teacher at school?
questions.sampleA1:
My teacher, Miss Lee. She is nice.

She teaches math.
questions.sampleA2:
My favourite teacher was Mr. Brown.

He taught history and it was interesting.

He was funny and I liked his class because it was not boring.
questions.sampleB1:
I think my favourite teacher was probably Mrs. Davis.

She taught us science, and she was really good at explaining things.

I liked her because she made science fun, with experiments and stuff.

Also, she was always very helpful if you didn't understand something, so I learned a lot.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose my favourite teacher would have to be my history teacher, Mr. Karimov. He had this knack for bringing the past to life instead of just making us memorise dates. The thing is, he genuinely believed in us, and he always went out of his way to help. He left a lasting impression on me.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Mening o'qituvchim, Miss Li. U yaxshi.

U matematika o'qitadi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Mening eng sevimli o'qituvchim janob Braun edi.

U tarix fanidan dars berardi va bu qiziqarli edi.

U hazilkash edi va menga uning darsi yoqardi, chunki u zerikarli emas edi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, eng sevimli o'qituvchim, ehtimol, Devis xonim edi.

U bizga fandan dars berardi va u narsalarni tushuntirishda juda yaxshi edi.

Menga u fanni qiziqarli qilgani uchun yoqardi, tajribalar va shunga o'xshash narsalar bilan.

Shuningdek, agar biror narsani tushunmasangiz, u har doim juda yordam berardi, shuning uchun men ko'p narsa o'rgandim.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Eslab qarasam, mening eng sevimli o'qituvchim geografiya fanidan dars bergan janob Harrison edi.

Uning fanga bo'lgan haqiqiy ishtiyoqi bor edi, bu uning darslarini qiziqarli va fikrlashga undaydigan qilib qo'yardi.

Menga eng ko'p yoqqan narsa uning geografik tushunchalarni iqlim o'zgarishi va globallashuv kabi real dunyo muammolari bilan bog'lay olishi edi.

U bizni tanqidiy fikrlashga va o'z fikrlarimizni shakllantirishga undardi, bu juda qimmatli edi.

Garchi mavzu murakkab bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, janob Harrison uni tushunarli va dolzarb qilib berardi.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Who was your favourite teacher at school?...

"Teach a man to fish, and you feed him for a lifetime" - "Insonni baliq ovlashga o'rgatsangiz, uni umrbod boqasiz"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Reflecting on my school days, my favourite teacher was undoubtedly Mr. Thompson. He taught English literature, and his classes were truly transformative. Mr. Thompson had an uncanny ability to bring stories to life, drawing in even the most disinterested students. What set him apart was his passion for storytelling and encouraging creativity. He would step into the shoes of literary characters, making every lesson a social experience that was far from conventional.

Mr. Thompson's influence on my love for literature was profoundly significant. He would often say, "The pen is mightier than the sword," inspiring us to explore the power of words. His teaching style was incredibly engaging; he used a mix of humor and critical thinking exercises which sparked off a curiosity in me that still thrives today.

Furthermore, he took time to mentor students outside the classroom, offering guidance and support in both academic and personal matters. I genuinely believe that his mentorship was a pivotal factor in my decision to pursue a career in writing. "A good teacher can inspire hope, ignite the imagination, and instill a love of learning," and Mr. Thompson exemplified this to perfection.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Maktab kunlarimni eslar ekanman, eng sevimli o'qituvchim, shubhasiz, janob Tompson edi. U ingliz adabiyotidan dars berardi va uning darslari haqiqatan ham o'zgartiruvchi edi. Janob Tompsonning hikoyalarni jonlantirish, hatto eng befarq o'quvchilarni ham jalb qilish qobiliyati g'ayrioddiy edi. Uni ajratib turadigan narsa hikoya qilishga bo'lgan ishtiyoqi va ijodkorlikni rag'batlantirishi edi. U adabiy qahramonlarning o'rniga o'zini qo'yardi va har bir darsni odatiy bo'lmagan ijtimoiy tajribaga aylantirardi.

Janob Tompsonning adabiyotga bo'lgan muhabbatimga ta'siri juda katta edi. U ko'pincha "Qalam qilichdan kuchliroq", der edi va bizni so'zlarning kuchini o'rganishga ilhomlantirardi. Uning o'qitish uslubi juda qiziqarli edi; u hazil va tanqidiy fikrlash mashqlaridan foydalanardi, bu esa menda bugungi kungacha saqlanib qolgan qiziqishni uyg'otdi.

Bundan tashqari, u sinfdan tashqari o'quvchilarga murabbiylik qilishga vaqt ajratar, akademik va shaxsiy masalalarda yo'l-yo'riq va yordam berardi. Men uning murabbiyligi yozuvchilik sohasida karera qilish qarorimda hal qiluvchi omil bo'lganiga chin dildan ishonaman. "Yaxshi o'qituvchi umid bag'ishlashi, tasavvurni uyg'otishi va o'rganishga muhabbatni singdirishi mumkin", va janob Tompson buni mukammal darajada namoyon etdi.

questions.sampleA1: My home? It is... good. I have a sofa. And a table. It is... blue.
questions.sampleA2: My home is okay. I have a sofa and a TV. The walls are white, and I have some pictures. It's small, but it's nice. I like my bed because it's comfortable.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think my home is quite comfortable. I have a living room with a sofa and a TV, of course. The kitchen is small, but it's functional. Also, I have some plants to make it feel more alive. In my opinion, it's a simple but nice place to live.
questions.sampleB2: Well, my place is pretty simple, to be honest. I've gone for a fairly minimalist look with neutral colours and not too much clutter. That said, I've added a few personal touches here and there, like framed photos and a couple of plants that brighten up the room. It's cosy, and it really feels like home.
questions.uzSampleA1: Mening uyim? U... yaxshi. Menda divan bor. Va stol. U... ko'k.
questions.uzSampleA2: Mening uyim yaxshi. Menda divan va televizor bor. Devorlar oq rangda, va menda ba'zi rasmlar bor. U kichkina, lekin u yoqimli. Menga karovatim yoqadi, chunki u qulay.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, menimcha, uyim juda qulay. Menda divan va televizor bor yashash xonasi bor, albatta. Oshxona kichkina, lekin u funksional. Shuningdek, u yanada jonliroq bo'lishi uchun ba'zi o'simliklarim bor. Mening fikrimcha, bu yashash uchun oddiy, ammo yaxshi joy.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Mening uyim juda oddiy, zamonaviy uslubda bezatilgan. Men minimalizmga moyilman, shuning uchun mebellar juda funksional va tartibli. Yumshoq yoritish va neytral ranglar palitrasi bilan dam oladigan muhit yaratishga harakat qildim.
Shunga qaramay, uyimga ko'proq iliqlik berish uchun san'at asarlari va fotosuratlar kabi shaxsiy teginishlarni ham qo'shdim.
Umuman olganda, menimcha, bu qulay va jozibali joy.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - How is your home decorated?...
idioms: home is where the heart is - "uy yurak joyi"
"Every wall tells a story" - "Har bir devor bir hikoya aytadi"
feather one's nest - "o'z uyini bezatmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Honestly speaking, I take immense pride in the way my home is adorned." - "Rostini aytsam, uyim qanday bezatilganidan juda faxrlanaman."
"From my perspective, the decor reflects a harmonious blend of modern and traditional elements." - "Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, dekor zamonaviy va an'anaviy elementlarning uyg'unligini aks ettiradi."
"I'd have to say that the aesthetic of my home is a reflection of my personal taste and style." - "Shuni aytishim kerakki, uyimning estetikasi mening shaxsiy didim va uslubimning aksidir."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Honestly, I take great pride in the way my home is decorated. It's a harmonious blend of modern and vintage styles that brings out the best of both worlds. As you step into the living room, you're greeted by a sleek sectional sofa that perfectly complements the minimalist coffee table. I've adorned the walls with abstract art pieces that add a splash of color and intrigue to the space.

Moving into the dining area, I've opted for a rustic wooden table paired with elegant chairs. The ambient lighting from the pendant lamps creates a warm and welcoming atmosphere, which is exactly what I aim for when hosting dinners. "Home is where the heart is," and I go the extra mile to ensure that every corner reflects my personality.

In the bedrooms, I have a more serene approach. Soft hues and plush fabrics dominate, creating a calm sanctuary. Interestingly, I came across some of the decor pieces while traveling, which not only serve as lovely reminders of those journeys but also inject a global flair into the overall look.

I take pleasure in rearranging and updating the decor occasionally, as it keeps things fresh and exciting. In essence, my home is a personal haven that reflects who I am and what I love.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, uyimning bezatilishiga katta e'tibor beraman. Bu zamonaviy va vintage uslublarning uyg'un aralashmasi bo'lib, ikkala dunyoning eng yaxshi tomonlarini ochib beradi. Mehmonxonaga kirishingiz bilan sizni minimalist jurnal stolini mukammal ravishda to'ldiradigan zamonaviy burchakli divan kutib oladi. Devorlarni rang-baranglik va qiziqish qo'shadigan abstrakt san'at asarlari bilan bezatdim.

Ovqatlanish xonasiga o'tsak, men nafis stullar bilan birlashtirilgan rustik yog'och stolni tanladim. Osma lampalardan tushadigan atrof-muhit yoritgichi iliq va yoqimli muhit yaratadi, bu esa kechki ovqatlarni tashkil qilganda aynan nimaga intilaman. "Uy - bu yurak joylashgan joy", va har bir burchak mening shaxsiyatimni aks ettirishini ta'minlash uchun bor kuchimni sarflayman.

Yotoq xonalarida esa, men yanada sokinroq yondashuvga egaman. Yumshoq ranglar va hashamatli matolar ustunlik qilib, tinch maskan yaratadi. Qizig'i shundaki, men sayohat paytida ba'zi dekorativ buyumlarga duch keldim, ular nafaqat o'sha sayohatlarning yoqimli eslatmalari bo'lib xizmat qiladi, balki umumiy ko'rinishga global ruh ham bag'ishlaydi.

Vaqti-vaqti bilan dekoratsiyani qayta tartibga solish va yangilashdan zavqlanaman, chunki bu narsalarni doimo yangi va hayajonli saqlaydi. Aslida, mening uyim - bu men kim ekanligimni va nimani yaxshi ko'rishimni aks ettiruvchi shaxsiy maskan.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
I see a woman.

She reads a book.

I see a room.
questions.sampleA2:
I see a woman and she is reading.

She is outside in the garden.

And I see another person reading in a room.

It is nice.
questions.sampleB1:
In the pictures, I can see people reading.

One woman is reading outside in a garden, I think.

The other person is reading inside their house, maybe.

Both pictures look very relaxing.

In my opinion, reading is good.
questions.sampleB2: So, both pictures show people relaxing with a book and a hot drink, but in quite different settings. In the first one, a young woman is sitting outdoors in a garden, engrossed in a paper book while sipping from a mug in the sunshine. She looks thoroughly content. The second picture, on the other hand, is indoors — someone's curled up in a cosy armchair reading an e-reader, with a candle flickering nearby. The thing is, both capture that same sense of calm, just one out in nature and the other tucked away at home.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Men bir ayolni ko'ryapman.

U kitob o'qiyapti.

Men bir xonani ko'ryapman.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men bir ayolni ko'ryapman va u o'qiyapti.

U tashqarida, bog'da.

Va men yana bir odamni xonada o'qiyotganini ko'ryapman.

Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Rasmlarda men odamlarni kitob o'qiyotganini ko'ryapman.

Bir ayol tashqarida, bog'da kitob o'qiyapti, menimcha.

Boshqa odam esa uyining ichida kitob o'qiyapti, balki.

Ikkala rasm ham juda xotirjam ko'rinadi.

Menimcha, kitob o'qish yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Rasmlarda odamlarning kitob o'qish orqali dam olishning ikki xil usuli ko'rsatilgan.

Bir rasmda bir ayol bog'da tashqarida kitob o'qib, quyosh nuridan bahramand bo'lmoqda.

Boshqa rasmda esa, kimdir qulay mehmonxonada ichkarida kitob o'qiyapti.

Ko'rinishidan, ikkala odam ham tinch vaqt o'tkazmoqda.

Ikkala muhit ham juda jozibali ko'rinadi va xotirjamlik hissini uyg'otadi.

Ko'rinib turibdiki, kitob o'qish - bu siz ichkarida ham, tashqarida ham zavq olishingiz mumkin bo'lgan sevimli mashg'ulot.

"From my perspective, these visuals offer a profound insight into the beauty and complexity of the world around us." - "Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, bu tasvirlar atrofimizdagi dunyoning go'zalligi va murakkabligini chuqur tushunishga imkon beradi."

"I'd have to say that these pictures are a testament to the artist's ability to capture the essence of their subject matter." - "Shuni aytishim kerakki, bu rasmlar rassomning mavzuning mohiyatini aks ettirish qobiliyatiga guvohlik beradi."

questions.sampleAnswer: "A picture is worth a thousand words," and these images bring to life the essence of relaxation and leisure in two distinct yet harmonious settings. In the first image, we see a woman enjoying a peaceful moment outdoors. She is comfortably seated on a wooden chair, with a good book in her lap and a cup in hand, suggesting she's "lost in a good book." The garden setting, with its greenery and blurred background of houses, creates an environment that is both serene and inviting. Her casual attire—a light blue sweater over a white top and jeans—along with her eyeglasses, contributes to a thoughtful and relaxed appearance. The presence of sunshine bathing the scene gently suggests a delightful spring or summer day, making it the perfect time to let her hair down and indulge in some leisure reading. The second image offers a different perspective on relaxation, yet it is equally inviting. Here, the individual is seated indoors in a cozy living room, deeply engaged with an e-reader. The presence of a white mug in one hand and a lit candle on the table adds to the warm and intimate atmosphere. The casual jeans and bracelets hint at a laid-back, at-home vibe. The sunlight streaming in through the window enhances the warmth of the room, creating a comforting and serene ambiance. This setting invites one to unwind and enjoy a quiet moment with a favorite book or story. Ultimately, both images capture the essence of finding solace in reading, whether it's outdoors amidst nature's embrace or indoors in the comfort of one's home. They highlight the importance of taking time for oneself, allowing for moments of reflection and relaxation in our busy lives.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
"Bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi," va bu rasmlar ikki xil, ammo uyg'un muhitda dam olish va hordiq chiqarish mohiyatini jonlantiradi.

Birinchi rasmda biz ochiq havoda tinch lahzadan bahramand bo'layotgan ayolni ko'ramiz. U yog'och stulda qulay o'tiribdi, tizzasida yaxshi kitob va qo'lida bir piyola bor, bu uning "kitobga berilib ketganini" ko'rsatadi. Bog' manzarasi, o'simliklari va xiralashgan uylar foni bilan, ham sokin, ham jozibali muhit yaratadi. Uning kundalik kiyimi - oq ustidagi och ko'k sviter va jinsi shimlar, ko'zoynaklari bilan birga, o'ychan va xotirjam ko'rinishga hissa qo'shadi. Quyoshning sahnani mayin yoritishi bahor yoki yozning ajoyib kunini ko'rsatadi, bu esa sochlarini yoyib, dam olish uchun o'qishga berilish uchun eng zo'r vaqt.

Ikkinchi rasm dam olishning boshqa nuqtai nazarini taqdim etadi, ammo u ham birdek jozibali. Bu yerda shaxs uy ichida, shinam yashash xonasida o'tiribdi, elektron kitob o'quvchi bilan chuqur mashg'ul. Bir qo'lida oq krujka va stol ustida yonayotgan shamning mavjudligi iliq va samimiy muhitga qo'shimcha qiladi. Kundalik jinsi shimlar va bilaguzuklar xotirjam, uy sharoitidagi kayfiyatdan dalolat beradi. Derazadan tushayotgan quyosh xonaning iliqligini oshiradi, taskin beruvchi va sokin muhit yaratadi. Bu muhit sevimli kitob yoki hikoya bilan sokin lahzadan bahramand bo'lishga chorlaydi.

Oxir-oqibat, ikkala rasm ham o'qishda taskin topish mohiyatini aks ettiradi, xoh u tabiat qo'ynida ochiq havoda bo'lsin, xoh uyning qulayligida bo'lsin. Ular band hayotimizda o'zimiz uchun vaqt ajratish, mulohaza va dam olish lahzalariga imkon berish muhimligini ta'kidlaydi.

questions.prompt: Which do you think is more enjoyable: reading a paper book or an eBook?
questions.sampleA1: I like paper book. It is good. I read it.
questions.sampleA2: I like paper books. They are nice and I can touch them. eBooks are okay too, but I like paper books more because it is easy.
questions.sampleB1: I think paper books are more enjoyable. You can hold them and it feels nice. eBooks are good too because you can carry many books. However, I prefer paper books because I like the way they smell and feel. In my opinion, it's just better to read a real book.
questions.sampleB2: For me, a paper book wins hands down. To be honest, there's something about the feel of the pages and even the smell that an e-reader just can't match. I suppose eBooks are handy when you're on the go, but nothing beats switching off and getting lost in a real book at the end of the day.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga qog'oz kitob yoqadi. U yaxshi. Men uni o'qiyman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men qog'oz kitoblarni yaxshi ko'raman. Ular yaxshi va men ularni ushlay olaman. Elektron kitoblar ham yaxshi, lekin menga qog'oz kitoblar ko'proq yoqadi, chunki u oson.
questions.uzSampleB1:

questions.sampleAnswer: In my opinion, reading a paper book is genuinely more enjoyable than reading an eBook. There's something about the tactile sensation of holding a book, turning the pages, and even the distinct smell of paper that eBooks simply can't replicate. "Old habits die hard," and I find that many people, myself included, gravitate towards the traditional format when it comes to enjoying literature. That being said, I certainly understand the appeal of eBooks. They're incredibly convenient, allowing you to carry an entire library in your pocket, which is a godsend when traveling. However, for the immersive experience, nothing beats sitting in a cozy corner with a good old paper book. Honestly, I believe this adds to the overall enjoyment and makes reading a truly special social experience.

Biroq, chuqur taassurot olish uchun, eski yaxshi qog'oz kitob bilan qulay burchakda o'tirishga hech narsa teng kelmaydi. questions.sampleAnswer:
In my opinion, while eBooks have undeniably grown in popularity and offer a plethora of advantages, they are unlikely to completely replace paper books in the foreseeable future. There is something remarkably special about the tactile experience of holding a paper book, turning its pages, and even enjoying the distinctive scent of the paper. This tactile pleasure is something that digital formats simply cannot live up to.

Moreover, paper books play a significant role in our cultural and educational systems. Libraries, for instance, have been integral parts of communities worldwide, and the experience of browsing through a library's physical collection can be a treasure trove of discoveries. For many, visiting a library or a bookstore is as much a social experience as it is an intellectual one.

That being said, eBooks offer unparalleled convenience and extensive accessibility. They allow people to carry thousands of books in a single device, which is incredibly convenient for avid readers or those who travel frequently. Their ability to be easily updated also makes them highly adaptable to contemporary needs.

In conclusion, while the digital format will continue to expand, I believe paper books will stand the test of time due to their aesthetic appeal and emotional connection they provide. After all, as the saying goes, "Old habits die hard."

Qog'oz kitobni ushlash, uning sahifalarini varaqlash va hatto qog'ozning o'ziga xos hididan bahramand bo'lishning o'zgacha bir sehrli tomoni bor. Bu taktil zavqni raqamli formatlar oddiygina qondira olmaydi.

Bundan tashqari, qog'oz kitoblar madaniy va ta'lim tizimlarimizda muhim rol o'ynaydi. Masalan, kutubxonalar butun dunyo bo'ylab jamiyatlarning ajralmas qismi bo'lib kelgan va kutubxonaning jismoniy to'plamini ko'zdan kechirish tajribasi kashfiyotlar xazinasiga aylanishi mumkin. Ko'pchilik uchun kutubxona yoki kitob do'koniga tashrif buyurish intellektual tajriba kabi ijtimoiy tajribadir.

Shunga qaramay, elektron kitoblar misli ko'rilmagan qulaylik va keng qamrovli imkoniyatlarni taqdim etadi. Ular odamlarga minglab kitoblarni bitta qurilmada olib yurishga imkon beradi, bu esa kitobxonlar yoki tez-tez sayohat qiladiganlar uchun juda qulaydir. Ularning oson yangilanishi ularni zamonaviy ehtiyojlarga juda moslashtiradi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, raqamli format kengayishda davom etsa-da, menimcha, qog'oz kitoblar o'zining estetik jozibasi va taqdim etadigan hissiy bog'liqligi tufayli vaqt sinovidan o'tadi. Axir, maqol bor: "Eski odatni tashlash qiyin".

questions.sampleB2: Okay, so the fear I'd probably say I overcame is my fear of public speaking. Honestly, for years it was something that absolutely terrified me. Even the thought of standing up in front of a room full of people would make my heart race and my hands go clammy. Back at university, I'd do almost anything to get out of giving a presentation — I'd swap topics, hide at the back, you name it. The thing is, in my final year I couldn't put it off any longer, because we had a huge group project to present in front of the whole department. I remember being an absolute bag of nerves the night before. So, rather than just bottling it up, I decided to face my fear head-on. I practised the whole thing over and over in front of the mirror, recorded myself on my phone, and even roped in a few friends to sit and be my practice audience so I could get used to all those eyes on me. When the big day came, I won't pretend it was easy — my voice was shaking at the start. But as I got into it, something just clicked, and by the end I was actually enjoying myself. To be honest, that experience completely turned things around for me. I suppose the lesson I took away was that the fear is nearly always worse in your head than in reality, and once you've actually done it, it loses its grip on you. Nowadays I still get butterflies, but I genuinely take it in my stride, and I'd never let a bit of nerves hold me back anymore.

bulletPoints: Share a time when you overcame a fear or faced something you were afraid of.
How has this experience affected your outlook on dealing with fear?
In what ways do fears shape people’s behaviors and decisions in society?
questions.sampleAnswer:
One of the most significant moments in my life when I faced up to a fear was when I decided to go skydiving. Although I have always been afraid of heights, the idea of jumping out of a plane at several thousand feet was extremely daunting. However, I knew that if I didn’t take the plunge, I would always feel limited by my fear.

As I stepped into the plane and soared higher into the sky, my heart raced, and I felt the adrenaline coursing through my veins. However, once I took that leap, a sense of freedom and exhilaration washed over me. It was then that I realized that fear is often just a barrier to incredible experiences. This experience has changed my outlook on dealing with fear, teaching me that courage is not the absence of fear but the willingness to act in spite of it.

In society, fears can profoundly influence people's behaviors and decisions. For instance, fear of failure might deter someone from pursuing their dreams, putting all their eggs in one basket by sticking to a safe career path instead of venturing out into something they genuinely love. Furthermore, fear of judgment might prevent individuals from expressing their true selves.

As "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself," learning to confront and overcome fears can be liberating, encouraging us to live more fulfilling lives. Ultimately, while fear can be a paralyzing force, it can also be a catalyst for personal growth and transformation when dealt with constructively.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening hayotimdagi qo'rquvga duch kelgan eng muhim lahzalardan biri bu osmondan sakrashga qaror qilganim bo'ldi. Garchi men doimo balandlikdan qo'rqqan bo'lsam ham, bir necha ming fut balandlikda samolyotdan sakrash g'oyasi juda qo'rqinchli edi. Biroq, agar men bu qadamni tashlamasam, doimo qo'rquvim bilan cheklangan bo'lib qolishimni bilardim.

Samolyotga qadam qo'yib, osmonga ko'tarilganimda, yuragim tez urdi va qon tomirlarimda adrenalinni his qildim. Biroq, o'sha sakrashni amalga oshirganimdan so'ng, erkinlik va hayajon hissi meni qamrab oldi. O'shanda men qo'rquv ko'pincha ajoyib tajribalarga to'siq bo'lishini angladim. Bu tajriba qo'rquvga qarshi kurashishga bo'lgan nuqtai nazarimni o'zgartirdi va menga jasorat qo'rquvning yo'qligi emas, balki unga qaramay harakat qilishga tayyorlik ekanligini o'rgatdi.

Jamiyatda qo'rquv odamlarning xatti-harakatlari va qarorlariga katta ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin. Misol uchun, muvaffaqiyatsizlikdan qo'rqish kimnidir o'z orzularini ro'yobga chiqarishdan to'xtatishi mumkin, o'zi chin dildan sevgan narsaga kirishish o'rniga, xavfsiz martaba yo'lida qolib, bor kuchini bir yo'nalishga sarflashi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, hukmdan qo'rqish odamlarni o'zligini ifoda etishga to'sqinlik qilishi mumkin.

"Qo'rqishimiz kerak bo'lgan yagona narsa - bu qo'rquvning o'zi", deganlaridek, qo'rquvga qarshi kurashish va uni yengishni o'rganish ozod qilishi, bizni yanada mazmunli hayot kechirishga undashi mumkin. Oxir oqibat, qo'rquv falajlovchi kuch bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, u konstruktiv tarzda hal etilganda, shaxsiy o'sish va o'zgarish uchun katalizator ham bo'lishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Animal testing should be banned worldwide.
questions.sampleA1:
Animals. Test. No good.

I think no.

Animals sad.

I think animal testing is bad.

Animals feel pain, and it's not fair.

Maybe we can find another way to test things, because I don't like animals to suffer.
questions.sampleB1:
I think animal testing is a difficult topic.

On the one hand, it can help us to find new medicines, for example, for diseases.

However, I also think it can be cruel to animals, and they might suffer.

So, in my opinion, we should try to find other ways to test things, but it's not easy.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so this is a really tricky one, and I can genuinely see both sides of the argument. On the one hand, the people who want animal testing banned have a point. It's hard to turn a blind eye to the fact that millions of animals are subjected to painful experiments every year, and many would say that causing that kind of suffering is simply cruel and morally wrong, especially when it's for something as trivial as cosmetics. On top of that, there are now alternatives — computer models, lab-grown tissue and so on — so the argument is that we shouldn't be falling back on outdated methods. Having said that, I think a worldwide ban would be a bit short-sighted. The thing is, a lot of life-saving medicines and vaccines have only come about thanks to animal research, and completely banning it overnight could do more harm than good. Those alternatives, brilliant as they are, can't yet fully replicate how a drug behaves in a living body, and until they can, scrapping animal testing entirely could set medical research back years. So, where do I stand? Personally, I don't think an outright ban is realistic just yet, but I'm firmly in favour of tightening the rules. I'd like to see far stricter regulation, testing only used as a last resort, and serious money poured into developing alternatives. In my view, that's the direction the whole world should be heading in. To be honest, I reckon that's the sensible middle ground — we phase it out gradually rather than pulling the plug all at once.

Shunday qilib, mening fikrimcha, biz narsalarni sinashning boshqa usullarini topishga harakat qilishimiz kerak, lekin bu oson emas.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazish murakkab masala bo'lib, har ikki tomonning ham kuchli argumentlari mavjud.

Bu hayvonlarga yetkazilgan azob-uqubatlar ularga nisbatan insonparvarlik bilan munosabatda bo'lish mas'uliyatimiz haqida jiddiy xavotirlarni uyg'otadi.

Bundan tashqari, hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazishning inson reaksiyalarini bashorat qilishdagi samaradorligi ko'pincha bahsga sabab bo'ladi va muqobil usullar tobora murakkablashib bormoqda.

Shuning uchun, menimcha, hayvonlarda sinov o'tkazmaslik usullarini ishlab chiqish va tasdiqlashga investitsiyalarni ko'paytirish bilan bir qatorda, butun dunyo bo'ylab taqiqlashni ko'rib chiqish kerak.

for: Animal testing is cruel and inhumane to animals.

questions.sampleAnswer:
"The greatness of a nation can be judged by the way its animals are treated." These words by Mahatma Gandhi really hit home in the context of the ongoing debate about animal testing. Honestly, the notion that animal testing should be banned is one I strongly support. First and foremost, the practice is cruel and inhumane to the animals involved. Many of these creatures are subjected to procedures that cause them immense pain, distress, or even death.

Moreover, with the rapid advancement of technology, alternatives to animal testing are becoming incredibly sophisticated. Computer models and in vitro methods offer viable options that figure out how substances interact with human biology without harming animals. In fact, these technologies often provide results that are more accurate and relevant to human physiology.

On the other hand, some argue that animal testing is crucial for the development of life-saving medicines and treatments. While it is undeniably true that certain breakthroughs have arisen from animal research, strict regulations can only go so far in ensuring humane treatment.

Furthermore, although some diseases may require animal testing to ensure safety, this practice should not be the be-all and end-all. We must step into a future where we don't put all our eggs in one basket and rely solely on animal testing. By prioritizing and investing in alternative methods, we can let our hair down knowing that science and ethics can walk hand in hand.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
"Millatning buyukligi uning hayvonlarga bo'lgan munosabati bilan baholanadi." Mahatma Gandining bu so'zlari hayvonlar ustida tajriba o'tkazish haqidagi davom etayotgan bahs kontekstida juda o'rinli. Rostini aytsam, hayvonlar ustida tajriba o'tkazishni taqiqlash kerak degan fikrni men qat'iy qo'llab-quvvatlayman. Avvalo, bu amaliyot hayvonlarga nisbatan shafqatsiz va insoniylikka zid. Bu mavjudotlarning ko'pchiligi ularga juda katta og'riq, azob yoki hatto o'lim keltiradigan muolajalarga duchor qilinadi.

Bundan tashqari, texnologiyaning tez rivojlanishi bilan hayvonlar ustida tajriba o'tkazishning muqobil usullari nihoyatda murakkablashib bormoqda. Kompyuter modellari va in vitro usullari hayvonlarga zarar yetkazmasdan turib, moddalarning inson biologiyasi bilan qanday o'zaro ta'sirlashishini aniqlaydigan maqbul variantlarni taklif etadi. Aslida, bu texnologiyalar ko'pincha inson fiziologiyasiga nisbatan aniqroq va tegishli natijalarni beradi.

Boshqa tomondan, ba'zilar hayvonlar ustida tajriba o'tkazish hayotni saqlab qoluvchi dori-darmonlar va davolash usullarini ishlab chiqish uchun juda muhim deb ta'kidlaydilar. Hayvonlar tadqiqotlari natijasida ma'lum yutuqlarga erishilgani shubhasiz to'g'ri bo'lsa-da, qat'iy qoidalar insonparvarlik munosabatini ta'minlashda unchalik yordam bermaydi.

Bundan tashqari, ba'zi kasalliklar xavfsizlikni ta'minlash uchun hayvonlar ustida tajriba o'tkazishni talab qilishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, bu amaliyot hamma narsaning asosi bo'lmasligi kerak. Biz faqat hayvonlar ustida tajriba o'tkazishga tayanib, barcha tuxumlarni bir savatga solmaydigan kelajakka qadam qo'yishimiz kerak. Muqobil usullarni ustuvorlashtirish va ularga sarmoya kiritish orqali biz fan va axloq birga qo'l ushlashib yurishini bilib, xotirjam bo'lishimiz mumkin.
